question: What will Adama Barrow’s margin be over his highest vote-getting opponent in the 2026 Gambian presidential election?

calls.reasoning: Anchor: the two prior Barrow elections had margins of +3.7 (2016) and +25.5 (2021); the 2021 poll understated his margin by about 6 points. The Aug 2026 Gambia Participates poll gives a raw +7, about +8.5 normalized. Kandeh and Faal endorsing Barrow plus the opposition split three ways (Darboe vs Bensouda) push the margin up; third-term backlash and NPP defections push it down. Polymarket (thin, about $10.5k volume) has Barrow to win at 0.79, which is consistent with roughly 15-18% for a margin of 0 or less. That is a who-wins contract, not a margin contract, so it is evidence only. No market on the margin was found. Centre of the distribution is about +10 to +12, with wide spread because Gambian polling is sparse.
calls.dossier:
- Election scheduled for 5 Dec 2026, single-round plurality; nominations ran 3-14 Nov 2026; about 1.1M registered voters (Anadolu, 11 Nov 2026).
- Candidates: Barrow (NPP, incumbent, third-term bid), Ousainou Darboe (UDP, 78, 'Gambia First'), Talib Bensouda (Unite/'Coalition 2026', KMC mayor), Bakary Badjie (independent), Mohamed Al Amin Bah (WAREF) (Wikipedia, Nov 2026).
- Poll, Gambia Participates, 27 Jul-10 Aug 2026, n=1,556: Barrow 32, Darboe 25, Bensouda 19, undecided 17. Perceived electability: Barrow 51 (up from 31 the previous round), Darboe 23, Bensouda 12. Regionally Barrow strongest in Basse, Darboe leads Mansakonko/Kerewan, Bensouda competitive in Kanifing/Brikama (Alkamba Times / Voice Gambia).
- Poll, CepRass, Jul 2025: Barrow 31, Bensouda 18, Darboe 12, undecided 29 (Wikipedia).
- 2021 precedent: CepRass Nov 2021 poll had Barrow 41, Darboe 22, Kandeh 6, Sallah 5. Actual result: Barrow 53.2, Darboe 27.7, so the poll understated Barrow's margin (raw 19 vs actual 25.5). A critic claims a 22-point underestimate; the poll got the winner right (Alkamba Times).
- 2016 result: Barrow 43.3 vs Jammeh 39.6 (+3.7).
- Mama Kandeh (GDC, about 12% in 2021) joined an NPP-led alliance in late July 2026, is not running, and campaigns for Barrow. Essa Faal (APP-Sobeyaa) also allied with Barrow, though his party has internal dissent (The Point; Timbuktu Institute, Oct 2026).
- Opposition unity talks (Coalition 2026) collapsed after UDP withdrew; the main obstacle is who would be the coalition candidate (Timbuktu Institute).
- Against Barrow: he broke his term-limits pledge; a survey says most Gambians don't want a third term; about 20 NPP officials defected to Kebba Madi Bojang's new NDP (Standard; Timbuktu).
- Status quo: Barrow wins by plurality against a split opposition. Event window: the election on 5 Dec 2026 -> results; per the fine print, 'Other result' if nothing resolves by 1 Jan 2027 (postponement or Barrow withdrawing).
- Resolves off official IEC results (or credible sources): Barrow's share minus the top opponent's share in percentage points.
- Searched, not found: any Oct/Nov 2026 poll; a betting market on the margin (only win markets exist).
calls.reference_class: Gambian presidential elections 2016 and 2021 (Barrow margins +3.7, +25.5), adjusted by the 2026 poll and 2021 poll-vs-result error

calls.reasoning: Anchor is 2021, when Barrow beat Darboe 53.2% to 27.7%, a 25.5-point margin, in a de facto two-way race. In 2026 the opposition is split between Darboe (UDP/Gambia First) and Bensouda (Coalition 2026), while Kandeh and Faal have joined Barrow. The August 2026 CepRass/Gambia Participates poll has Barrow 32, Darboe 25, Bensouda 19, Faal 3, Kandeh 2, with 17% undecided. Excluding undecided and adding Faal and Kandeh to Barrow implies a margin of about 15 points. Incumbency and rural turnout have historically helped Barrow beat his polling (from memory, not checked), which supports the 20+ bucket. A Bensouda surge or UDP consolidation keeps the 0-10 and <=0 buckets live. Polymarket has Barrow at 79% to win (about $10.5k volume; a who-wins contract, not a margin contract), consistent with a 17% chance he trails. Other result is small because the election is December 5, well before the January 1 cutoff.
calls.dossier:
- Election date is Dec 5, 2026. About 1.1M registered voters. Nominations ran Nov 3-14, 2026 (Anadolu, Nov 11, 2026). Voting is by marble, with no runoff (plurality wins).
- Main candidates: Barrow (NPP, incumbent, seeking a 3rd term; no term limits after the constitutional amendment failed), Ousainou Darboe (UDP, 78, leads the 'Gambia First' bloc), Talib Bensouda (UNITE/Coalition 2026, 40, Kanifing mayor). Also Bakary Badjie (independent) and Mohamed Al Amin Bah (Wikipedia; The Point, Nov 2026).
- Mama Kandeh (GDC) joined/allied with the NPP in late July 2026. Essa Faal allied with Barrow (Timbuktu Institute, Oct 2026). NUP joined a 'Team Gambia Grand Coalition' (The Point).
- About 20 NPP officials defected to the new NDP led by Kebba Madi Bojang (Timbuktu, Oct 2026).
- Efforts to unite the opposition stalled over who would be the candidate (Timbuktu, Oct 2026).
- CepRass/Gambia Participates poll, Jul 27-Aug 10, 2026, n=1,556, all 53 constituencies: Barrow 32, Darboe 25, Bensouda 19, Faal 3, Kandeh 2, others 2, undecided 17. 51% say Barrow has the best chance of winning. A majority reportedly oppose a third term. Regional picture: Barrow strongest in Basse; Darboe leads Mansakonko and Kerewan; Bensouda competitive in Kanifing and Brikama (Alkamba Times; Standard). Opposition parties dispute the poll (The Point).
- There was an earlier CepRass first-round poll in Aug 2025, same sample size; its figures were not found.
- 2021 result: Barrow 53.2%, Darboe 27.7%, Kandeh about 12%, margin about 25.5 points. 2016 result: Barrow (coalition) 43.3% vs Jammeh 39.6%, margin about 3.7 points.
- A lecturer told Bloomberg (Nov 2026) that a divided opposition has historically helped the incumbent.
- Status quo: incumbent against a split opposition. Margin is measured between Barrow and whoever finishes second.
- Resolves off official IEC results or credible sources, as Barrow's share minus the top opponent's share. 'Other result' applies if nothing resolves by Jan 1, 2027 (postponement or withdrawal).
- Event window: election Dec 5, 2026 -> results expected within days; deadline Jan 1, 2027. As of Nov 13, 2026, the vote has not happened.
- Searched for but not found: any polls after August 2026, and evidence on how accurate Gambian polls were in 2021.
calls.reference_class: Gambian presidential elections with Barrow as incumbent or frontrunner (2016 margin about 3.7 points against Jammeh; 2021 margin about 25.5 points against Darboe), adjusted by the 2026 voting-intention poll

calls.reasoning: Prior from Barrow's prior margins (2016 ~+4 vs Jammeh, 2021 +25.5 vs Darboe). Kandeh (12% in 2021) and Faal (4.5%) now endorse Barrow while the opposition is split between Darboe and Bensouda, which favours a large margin. The only vote-intention poll (Gambia Participates, Aug 2026: 32/25/19, 17% undecided) implies roughly a 9-pt margin after normalizing, and third-term unpopularity and defections pull downward. Polymarket's 0.79 Barrow-win price (~$10.5k volume; prices the winner, not the margin) supports roughly 20% on a loss. Spread across bins with a modest lean to a larger margin, in line with the incumbency pattern seen in 2021.
calls.dossier:

- IEC confirmed 5 candidates: Barrow (NPP), Darboe (UDP), Bensouda (UNITE), Dr Isatou Touray (independent), Modou Lamin Sima (APC); NDP and GLP nominations rejected (Kerr Fatou, Nov 2026).
- 2021 result: Barrow 53.2%, Darboe 27.7% (margin ~25.5 pts); Kandeh ~12%, Faal ~4.5% (Wikipedia). 2016: Barrow ~43.3 vs Jammeh ~39.6 (margin ~3.7), from background knowledge.
- Kandeh joined NPP in late July 2026; Essa Faal (APP-Sobeyaa) endorsed Barrow; Barrow says their combined 2021 votes ensure his win (Timbuktu Institute, Oct 2026).
- Opposition split: Darboe leads 'Gambia First', Bensouda leads 'Coalition 2026'; merger talks stalled (Timbuktu, Oct 2026).
- ~20 NPP officials defected to NDP; dissent inside APP-Sobeyaa over the Faal alliance (Timbuktu, Oct 2026).
- Gambia Participates poll, Aug 2026, n=1,556: Barrow 32, Darboe 25, Bensouda 19, undecided 17 (VoiceGambia). A November round has 51% saying Barrow has the best chance of winning, up from 31%.
- Gambia Participates, July 2025: 55% oppose a third term; 60% said they would not vote for Barrow (Alkamba Times).
- Barrow broke his pledge not to seek a third term; parliament rejected a term-limit amendment in 2025 (Bloomberg via WowTV, 2026-11-11).
- A UTG lecturer says a divided opposition has historically helped the incumbent (Bloomberg, Nov 2026).
- Polymarket has winner markets only; no margin market found.
- Resolves off the official/credible vote-share gap between Barrow and the second-placed candidate. Event window: election 5 Dec 2026; 'Other' only if no result before 1 Jan 2027. Searched for but not found: an independent second pollster, November vote-intention numbers.
calls.reference_class: Gambian presidential elections with Barrow as candidate (2016, 2021), plus incumbent-vs-fragmented-opposition West African elections

calls.reasoning: Only vote-intention poll (Aug 2026): Barrow 32, Darboe 25, Bensouda 19, 17% undecided -> ~+8 normalized, ~+14.5 once Kandeh/Faal backers (now allied with Barrow) are reallocated; 2021 the same pollster understated Barrow's margin by ~6 pts. Split opposition (Darboe vs Bensouda, possibly Touray) in a single-round plurality race widens the winner's lead over the runner-up. Third-term unpopularity and defections keep a loss live (~16%, consistent with Polymarket winner price 0.79, a who-wins contract only, thin volume). Centre ~+15 with wide spread.
calls.reconciliation: Factual dispute over the candidate list (Run 3: IEC confirmed Touray and Sima; Runs 1-2: Badjie and Bah) could not be checked without web access; it matters little because minor candidates mostly split the opposition. The main judgment dispute is poll weight vs the 2021 precedent. Normalizing the Aug 2026 poll and reallocating the Kandeh/Faal share gives ~+14.5, and adjusting for the ~6-pt understatement seen in 2021 puts the centre near +15-18, above Run 1's +10-12. That shifts weight toward the 10-20 and 20+ bins, while third-term backlash keeps ~16% on a loss. Carried forward the runs' reference class. Polymarket's winner contract is a near-miss, used as evidence only.
